title: Лист орендодавцю про несправність
task: Напишіть власнику квартири: уже два дні не працює опалення (або протікає кран). Опишіть проблему, попросіть швидко прислати майстра і запропонуйте зручний час.

items: I'm writing to let you know that…
The heating hasn't been working since Monday.
It is getting quite cold in the flat.
I have tried … but it did not help.
Could you please send someone to fix it as soon as possible?
I am available on … after 5 pm.
Please let me know when would suit you.
I look forward to hearing from you.

sample:
Dear Mr Kowalski,

I hope you are well. I'm writing to let you know that the heating in our flat hasn't been working since Monday. We have checked the thermostat and restarted the boiler, but it didn't help, and it is getting quite cold, especially at night.

Could you please send someone to fix it as soon as possible? We are at home every day after 5 pm and all day on Saturday. Please let me know when would suit you.

Thank you in advance.

Best regards,
Pavlo

title: Запрошення друга на вихідні

items: We're having a barbecue at our place.
Do you fancy going hiking in the Tatras?
It would be great to catch up.

Let me know if you can make it!

Long time no see! Are you free on Saturday? We're having a barbecue at our place from around 4 pm. A few friends from work are coming too, and it would be great to catch up. Just bring something to drink — we'll take care of the food. We can pick you up if you like.

Let me know if you can make it!
Cheers,

title: Скарга в інтернет-магазин
task: Ви отримали замовлення, але товар пошкоджений (або прийшов не той розмір). Напишіть у службу підтримки: номер замовлення, що не так, чого ви хочете (заміна чи повернення грошей).

items: I am writing to complain about my recent order (No. …).
The package was opened when it arrived.
I would like a replacement as soon as possible.
I would prefer a full refund.
Could you please arrange a free return?
I look forward to your reply.

Dear Customer Service,

I am writing to complain about my recent order (No. 48213), which arrived yesterday. Unfortunately, the coffee machine was damaged — the water tank is cracked, and water leaks out as soon as I fill it. The box itself looked fine, so it was probably damaged before it was packed. I have attached some photos.

I would prefer a full refund rather than a replacement. Could you please arrange a free return?

I look forward to your reply.

Kind regards,
Pavlo Zhyhalov

title: Відгук про ресторан або готель
task: Напишіть відгук на TripAdvisor / Google про місце, де ви нещодавно були: що сподобалося, що ні, кому порадите.

items: We had dinner here last Friday.
Overall, we had a great time.
It was a bit disappointing, to be honest.
The staff were friendly and helpful.
It is a bit pricey, but worth it.
Make sure you book a table in advance.

sample:
We had dinner here last Friday to celebrate our anniversary. The food was delicious, especially the duck, and the staff were friendly and helpful. Our waiter even brought us a small dessert with a candle, which was a lovely surprise. The only downside was that the service was quite slow when it got busy.

It's a bit pricey, but definitely worth it. Perfect for a special occasion — just make sure you book a table in advance, especially at the weekend.

title: Запит про курс або послугу

items: I am writing to enquire about…
Could you tell me when the classes start?
How much does the course cost?
Is it possible to join a trial lesson?
I would be grateful for any further information.

Could you tell me when the next course starts, how long it lasts and how much it costs? Are there any discounts for couples? As we both work full-time, only evening or weekend classes would suit us. Also, is it possible to join a trial lesson first?

title: Робоче: запит ціни постачальнику

Please let me know if you need any further information.

I am writing on behalf of our company, a bicycle manufacturer based in Kraków. We are looking for a reliable supplier of machined aluminium parts. Could you please send us a quote for 500 pieces of the part in the attached drawing (material 6061-T6, anodized black)? title: Есе: віддалена робота
task: Напишіть есе (200–250 слів): «Віддалена робота приносить більше користі, ніж шкоди». Наведіть аргументи за і проти, визнайте слабкі місця своєї позиції і зробіть зважений висновок.

items: On balance, I would argue that…

sample:
In recent years, remote work has shifted from a rare perk to a mainstream arrangement. While it undoubtedly offers significant advantages, its drawbacks are often underestimated.

One compelling argument in its favour is flexibility. Without a daily commute, employees regain hours that can be devoted to family, rest or personal development. Moreover, companies are able to recruit talent regardless of location, which arguably broadens opportunities on both sides. Many employees also report being more productive at home, where there are fewer interruptions than in an open-plan office.

Admittedly, remote work is not without its problems. Spontaneous collaboration suffers, and new employees in particular may struggle to learn without colleagues to observe. Isolation can also take a toll on mental health, blurring the line between work and private life.

Having said that, most of these issues stem from poor implementation rather than from remote work itself. Regular in-person meetings, clear communication norms and deliberate onboarding can mitigate many of the risks.

On balance, I would argue that the benefits outweigh the costs, provided that organisations treat remote work as a system to be designed rather than an emergency measure. A hybrid model, combining autonomy with regular face-to-face contact, appears to offer the best of both worlds.

title: Офіційний лист до міської ради
task: Напишіть лист до міської ради (180–220 слів) з пропозицією облаштувати велодоріжку на вашій вулиці. Опишіть проблему, обґрунтуйте користь, запропонуйте конкретне рішення.

items: As a resident of… for several years,…
This poses a significant risk to…
Not only would this…, but it would also…
I would be grateful if you could consider…
I look forward to your response.

sample:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing as a resident of Lipowa Street to propose the construction of a dedicated cycle lane along its full length.

At present, cyclists are forced to share a narrow road with heavy traffic, including delivery lorries serving the nearby industrial area. This poses a significant risk, particularly to children cycling to the two schools located on the street. Several near-misses have been reported this year alone.

A separated cycle lane would not only improve safety but would also encourage more residents to leave their cars at home, thereby reducing congestion and noise. Similar lanes introduced in other districts of Kraków have proved both popular and effective. Given that the pavement on the eastern side is unusually wide, the lane could be introduced at relatively low cost, without reducing the number of parking spaces.

I would be grateful if you could consider including this project in next year's budget. Many of my neighbours share this view, and we would be happy to take part in any public consultation.

I look forward to your response.

Yours faithfully,
Pavlo Zhyhalov

title: Звіт про покращення в місті
task: Міський портал просить мешканців оцінити нещодавнє покращення в місті (нові велодоріжки, оновлена бібліотека, нічні трамваї тощо). Напишіть звіт із підзаголовками: що змінилося, що вдалося, що ні, і ваші рекомендації.

items: The aim of this report is to assess…
This report is based on my own experience and conversations with…
Introduced last spring, the scheme was intended to…
The most noticeable improvement has been…
This has proved particularly popular with…
However, a number of issues remain.
In light of the above, I would recommend…
Overall, the scheme has been a success, although…

sample:
Night Trams in Kraków: A Resident's Report

Introduction
The aim of this report is to assess the night tram service introduced last spring. It is based on my own experience and on conversations with neighbours and friends who use it regularly.

What has changed
Previously, public transport stopped shortly before midnight, leaving taxis as the only option. Four tram lines now run every thirty minutes until 4 am at weekends.

What has worked well
On the positive side, the service has made the city centre far more accessible in the evenings. It has proved particularly popular with students and hospitality staff, many of whom finish work late and previously spent a considerable part of their wages on taxis. The trams are clean, and the presence of security staff has made passengers feel noticeably safer.

What has not
However, a number of issues remain. The service does not yet reach several large residential districts, so many residents still face a long walk home. In addition, timetable information at stops is often out of date, which causes unnecessary frustration.

Recommendations
In light of the above, I would recommend extending at least one line to the outer districts and introducing live departure boards at the busiest stops. It would also be advisable to run the service on Thursday nights.

Conclusion
Overall, the scheme has been a success, although it will only reach its full potential once these gaps are addressed.

sample: Three years ago, Vita and I went to the mountains in Georgia. It was our first big trip together, and we had planned everything carefully. Looking back, that trip taught me that the best moments are often the ones you don't plan. We still laugh about it.

title: Офіційна скарга до служби доставки

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about the delivery of my parcel (tracking number PL4829105). The parcel was due to arrive on 3 March, but it was not delivered until 7 March, despite several messages from your company confirming the original date.

What is more, the courier did not ring the bell or call me, even though I was at home all day. Instead, he left the parcel outside the building in the rain. I expect to receive a reply within 14 days. If the matter is not resolved, I will have no choice but to take it further with the consumer protection office.

Yours faithfully,
Pavlo

title: Есе: соцмережі для дітей
task: Напишіть есе-думку: чи варто дозволяти дітям до 13 років користуватися соцмережами? Наведіть аргументи за і проти, підтримайте їх прикладами і сформулюйте власну позицію.

items: This raises the question of whether…
However, this does not mean that…
All in all, I believe that…

sample:
Nowadays, more and more children own a smartphone before they turn ten. This raises the question of whether they should be allowed to use social media at such a young age. In my view, it is better for them to wait.

On the one hand, social media can help children stay in touch with friends and discover new interests. For example, a shy child might find others who love the same music or games. What is more, parents sometimes argue that banning these apps only makes children want them more.

On the other hand, the risks are serious. Young children are not yet able to deal with online bullying, unrealistic images or contact with strangers. Many apps are also designed to be addictive, which can affect sleep, concentration and even self-esteem.

While it may be true that children will meet social media sooner or later, this does not mean they need to start at eight or nine. To sum up, I believe children under thirteen should wait, and parents should introduce social media gradually and with clear rules.

title: Рекомендаційний лист для друга

Dear Ms Nowak,

I am writing to recommend Taras Melnyk as a tenant for your flat. I have known Taras for over eight years. We first met at university in Lviv, and since moving to Kraków we have remained close friends.

Taras is one of the most reliable and responsible people I know. He always pays his bills on time and keeps his promises, however small. For instance, when my wife and I were away for a month last summer, Taras looked after our flat. He watered the plants, checked the post and even fixed a dripping tap without being asked.

He is also quiet, tidy and considerate. He gets on well with everyone in his current building, and his neighbours often ask him for help. In addition, he has a stable job as an accountant, so I have no doubt that he can afford the rent.

Pavlo

sample:
Kraków: A City That Grows on You

When I first arrived in Kraków with my wife three years ago, I expected to stay for a year at most. Three years on, we're still here — and, to our own surprise, we're thinking of raising a family here.

What struck me most at the beginning was how compact the city is. You can cross the Old Town on foot in fifteen minutes, yet every street seems to hide a courtyard café, a bookshop or a tiny gallery. Locals may seem reserved at first, but once you've been invited to someone's name-day party, you'll realise how warm they really are.

Much as I love the city, I can't help being irritated by a few things. The smog in winter can be genuinely unpleasant, and the trams, while cheap, are packed at rush hour. Paperwork is another story altogether: be prepared to visit the same office more than once.

If I could give newcomers one piece of advice, it would be to learn at least some Polish. Even a few clumsy phrases will open doors that English alone cannot. It's also well worth getting out of the centre: Kazimierz and Podgórze have a character of their own, and the lake at Zakrzówek is perfect on a hot summer day. Don't be put off by the grey November weather either — that's exactly when the cafés feel cosiest.

All in all, Kraków rewards patience. Give it time, and you might just find that it stops feeling like a stopover and starts feeling like home.

Proposal: Bringing Our Courtyard Back to Life

Introduction
The purpose of this proposal is to suggest how the courtyard behind our building could be turned into a pleasant shared space. At present, it is used mainly as an informal car park. The playground equipment is rusty and, in places, unsafe, and there is nowhere to sit. Many residents, particularly families and older neighbours, have expressed concern about this.

Proposed changes
Firstly, I would propose limiting parking to the marked spaces along the wall, which would free up the central area. Secondly, the old climbing frame should be replaced with a small, certified play area on a safe rubber surface. Finally, we could add four benches, two bike racks and a few raised flower beds that residents could look after together. This would not only make the courtyard safer, but also give neighbours a reason to meet and get to know each other.

Cost and possible objections
The estimated cost is around 45,000 zł. This could be partly funded by the city's participatory budget, with the remainder covered by our renovation fund over two years. It could be argued that drivers would lose convenient spaces; however, only three cars currently park outside the marked bays, and there are free spaces in the street nearby.

Next steps
I would therefore suggest that the proposal be put to a vote at the next residents' meeting. As a first step, I would be happy to collect quotes from contractors and prepare a simple plan.

sample:
Klara and the Sun by Kazuo Ishiguro

Kazuo Ishiguro's Klara and the Sun is narrated by Klara, an "Artificial Friend" — a solar-powered robot bought as a companion for Josie, a lonely and often unwell teenager. Without giving too much away, the novel follows Klara as she tries to understand the family she has joined and to protect the girl she has come to care for.

What makes the book stand out is its narrator. Klara observes the world with a mixture of precision and innocence, and Ishiguro handles this limited point of view with remarkable subtlety. We often understand more than she does, which makes her loyalty all the more heartbreaking. Her almost religious faith in the Sun, which she believes can heal, is one of the most original ideas I have come across in recent fiction. At its heart, the novel is a quiet but deeply moving reflection on love, loneliness and what makes a person irreplaceable.

That said, the pace occasionally drags, particularly in the first third, where Klara's careful descriptions of the shop can feel repetitive. Some readers may also find the world-building frustratingly vague: key elements of this future society are hinted at but never fully explained. My only real reservation, however, is that the ending, though beautiful, feels slightly rushed.

On balance, this is a thoughtful, elegant and memorable novel rather than a gripping one. I would wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone who enjoys slow, reflective fiction and is willing to read between the lines. Four stars out of five.
